result.scope_note: Under the HTTP/2 specification (RFC 9113) and HTTP/1.1 (RFC 7230/7231), a 200 HEAD response MUST NOT include a message body, while a 200 GET response MUST include the full representation. Therefore the claim is true: a 200 GET response always carries body bytes where a 200 HEAD response carries zero bytes for the same nonempty resource.

1. excerpts.text: *HTTP 200 (OK)* is the standard success answer, and it means the request worked. It is the most common answer on the web. What comes in the body depends on the request: for a *GET* it is the requested data, and for other methods it describes the result. The rule is defined in [RFC 9110 section 15.3.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-15.3.1), the official HTTP specification.
